text: True or False: Exhibiting a single value x for which P(x) holds is sufficient to prove the universal statement ∀x P(x).
explanation: False. One confirming example proves only the existential ∃x P(x), not the universal ∀x P(x); a universal requires an argument covering every x (typically a proof about an arbitrary x). A single example does, however, suffice to disprove a universal, serving as a counterexample — the reverse situation.
